Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

0. FOREWORD 



M Thii Indian Stmndard ( Second Revision } 
wet adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards 
on 2 May 1988, after the draft finalized by the 
Handloom and Khadi Sectional Committee had 
been approved by the Textile Division Council. 

0.2 This standard was first published in 1956 
and revised in 1969. It has been again taken 
up for re^sion in order to align it with the 
specification laid down by Government of India 
ior surgical dressinm and notified and given at 
the Schedule F( II } in the Drugs and Cosmetics 
(First Amendment) Rules 1984. Other impor- 
tant changes carried out are as under: 

a) Deletion of breaking load requirements 
since cotton yam conforming to IS : 171- 
1985* has been specified. 

b) In order to determine conformity of 



bandage cloth to the requirements of this 
standard, it is permitted to carry out con- 
ditioning and testing of samples in the 
prevailing atmospheric conditions. How- 
ever, in sul cases of disputes, conditioning 
and testing shall be carried out in standard 
atmospheric conditions as envisaged in 
the referred Indian Standards on test 
methods. 

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a 
particular requirement of this standard is 
complied with, the final value, observed or 
calculated, expressing the result of a test or 
analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the 
same as that of the specified value in this 
standard.

1. SCOPE 

!•! This standard prescribes the constructional 
particulars* and other requirements for hand- 
loom cotton bandage cloth, bleached and 
non-steriUaed. 

^MANVFACroRB 

2.1 Yasm — Cotton yarn conforming to IS^ 171- 
1985* shaU be used. 



ZIZ dotli — The cloth shall be woven in plain 
weave with well formed selvedge and free from 
weaving defects. It shall also be flree from 
filling, siiing or dressing material. The cloth 
shall also be bleached. 

2.2.1 If agreed to between the buyer and the 
seller, the bandage cloth may be cut according 
to the agreed dimension and supf^ed in rofl 



*Sp«dficatioii for* cotton and cotton r«gsnerattd 
edluloiic fibra bitadwl groy yarn (tMrdrmrim). 



form. The selvedge shall not be included in cut 
bandages. Both the extreme edges shaU be 
straight and evenly cut with reasonable freedom 
from loose threads. 

3. REQUIREMENTS 

3.1 The bandage cloth shall conform to the 
requirements specified in Table 1 . 

4. PACKING 

4»1 Bandage cloth shall be packed securely so 
as to allow normal handling and tranq>ort 
without tearing and exposing the contents. In 
case of cut and rolled bandages each bandage 
shall be wrapped in a suitable paper. Details of 
the packing uiall be as agreed to between the 
buyer and the seller. 

4.1.1 A suitable packing procedure is given in 
Appendix A for information and guidance.

5. MARKING 

5.1 E^ch packet of bandage cloth shall be legibly 
marked with the following information: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade- 
mark, if any; 

c) Month and year of manufacture; 

d) Length ( m ) and width ( cm ); and 

e) The words *NOT STERILIZED'. 

5.1.1 The bandage cloth may also be marked 
with the Standard Mark. 

NoTK — The use of the Standard Mark is governed 
by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act 
19Bb and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 



The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian 
Standard conveys the assurance that they have been 
pfoduced to comply with the requirements of that 
standard under a well defined system of insMtioii, 
testing and quality control which is devised and super- 
vised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard 
marked products are also continuously checked by BIS 
for conformity to that standard as a further lafeouard. 
Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
o: the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
of producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian 
Standards. 

6. SAMPLING AND COUTERIA FOR CON- 
FORMTTY 

6.1 To ascertain the conformity of the test to 
the requirements of this standard the procedure 
given in IS : 9710-1981* shall be followed for 
sampling and inspection.

APPENDIX A 

( Clause 4.1.1 ) 

PROGE1H7RE FOR PACKING HANOLOOM COTTON BANDAGE 
CLOTH AND CUT BANDAGES 



A-1* The bandage doth, tuitably folded one 
over the other, shall be wrapped with two layers 
of kraft paper (sm IS :. 139^1967*). 

A"2. Cut bandages shall be made into rolls 
( dressings }. Each dressing shall be neatly and 
securely wrapped with blue or brown paper 
wrapping around its circumference only leavmg 
the ends uncovered. Ten ( or twenty in case of 
smaller size, for example, 2*5 cm width) such 
dressings shall then be wrapped in kraft paper 
( stt : 1397-l%7* ) to form a packet. The packet 
shall be securely glued or gummed at each 
end. 

A-3. The packets as obtained in A-1 and A-2 

shall be wrapped with the following materials: 

a) One layer of waterproof (iff IS: 1398- 
1982t) 



One layer of polyethylene film of 40 



micron thickness ( su Grade 123 of IS : 
2508-1984*). 

Waterproof paper or polyethylene film 
shaU have an overlap of at least 15 cm. 

b) One layer of hessian conforming to type 1 
ofIS:2818(Part2)-1971t. 

AHl The outer layer of bale, that is, the hessian, 
shall be securely sewn with at least 12 stitches 
per decimeter. The slats of timber approximately 
80 mm wide and 12 mm thick shall be placed 
lengthwise along the edges of the bale and three 
steel baling hoops shall be used to tighten the 
bale and hold the slats in position. Tae hoops 
shall preferably be machine sealed and made 
from the rivets. 

A-A. Unless otherwise specified, the gross weight 
of bale shall not exceed 37 kg. 

A*^ Press packing of bale shall be carried out« 
wherever possible.

tSpecification for packing paper, waterproof, bitumen 
laminated (steondrivistoH), 



^Specification for low dennty polyethylene films ( immi4 
rwUimt ). 

tSpecification for Indian heiiian ( 305 and 229 g/m* at 
16 percent contract regain ) (Jirst rgoUimt ).
